segments.text: Hi Robert, thanks so much for joining. I'm Nadia, your customer success manager, and this is Ethan from our product team.
Hi Robert, great to meet you. I'm really grateful for the time. Mostly I want to listen today and learn how your team works.
Happy to help. Fair warning, I've got a hard stop in about thirty minutes, so I'll try to be efficient.
That's plenty. Let's start simple. Can you walk me through what a normal day looks like for your dispatch team?
Sure. We run about two hundred trucks across the Midwest, and every morning my dispatchers rebuild the day's routes by hand from three different spreadsheets.
Three spreadsheets. What's in each one?
One has customer orders, one has driver availability, and one has maintenance schedules. None of them talk to each other.
And how long does that rebuild take each morning?
Usually two to three hours. By the time routes go out, we're already behind on the first deliveries.
That's a big chunk of the day. What happens when something changes after the routes go out?
That's the real headache. A driver calls in sick or a truck breaks down, and my dispatchers start calling people and rewriting the plan on the fly.
Last month a single breakdown cost us four late deliveries and one very unhappy grocery customer.
I remember that escalation. It came through our support queue.
Right. That one hurt.
If you could wave a wand, what would the ideal morning look like?
Routes build themselves from the order system, and when something changes, my team gets a suggested fix they can approve with one click.
So the human stays in control, but the busywork disappears.
Exactly. I don't want a black box making decisions. I want a smart assistant that my dispatchers trust.
That's very consistent with what other logistics customers have told us.
Can I ask about the approval part? Who would need to sign off on a route change today?
Usually the shift supervisor. For anything over a certain cost, say a hundred and fifty dollars in extra mileage, it comes to me.
That's interesting. So approvals are tiered by cost.
Yes, and if your tool can't handle that, it's not going to work for us.
Understood. I'm writing that down as a hard requirement, tiered approvals based on cost.
Robert, what other tools does your team rely on that we'd need to connect with?
We use a fleet telematics platform for truck locations, and an old but reliable order management system.
If we can't pull data from both, you're asking my team to type everything in again, and they won't do that.
That makes sense. Do you have an engineer or an administrator who could help us with the technical setup?
I have one very patient person named Dana in our IT group. I can introduce you.
That would be wonderful. I'll follow up with Dana after this call.
One more question. How do you measure success for your team today?
On time delivery rate, mostly. We're at ninety-one percent right now, and my goal is ninety-six by the end of next year.
And how much of the gap do you think comes from late route changes?
More than half, honestly. The morning rebuild and the mid-day scrambles are where we lose most of it.
Then there's a clear link between what we're discussing and the outcome you care about.
That's why I agreed to this call. If this works, I can make the case to my executives.
That's really helpful. What would you need to see to feel confident in a pilot?
A small pilot with one depot, maybe thirty trucks, for about six weeks, with a clear way to compare against our current numbers.
We can absolutely set that up. I'll draft a pilot plan and send it to you by next Friday.
And I'll send you a short prototype of the approval flow next week, so you can tell us if we got the tiers right.
That would be great. Honestly, this is the first vendor call where somebody asked about my day instead of pitching me.
That means a lot, Robert. Thank you for being so open with us.
We'll be in touch soon. Have a great rest of your day.

action_items.task: Draft the Northwind pilot plan for one depot and send it to Robert
Send Robert a prototype of the cost based approval flow
Follow up with Dana in IT about telematics and order system access

clips.title: Why morning route rebuilds cost Northwind so much
